findings.title: traceID is no longer logged with plugin request completion events
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly appended a "traceID" field from tracing.TraceIDFromContext, plus pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName and dsUID. The new code removes all of these and only calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname, but not traceID. Unless the infra logger injects the trace ID itself (nothing in this diff shows that), completion logs lose the trace ID, which breaks log-to-trace correlation for plugin requests. The PR is titled and described as a rename, so this user-visible logging change is not called out.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops all contextual attributes when the type assertion fails
findings.body: FromContext does d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger) and, on failure, falls back to d.New() with no context. If the infra logger ever returns a different concrete type (wrapper, interface change), every LoggerMiddleware log line silently loses the plugin/datasource/user context that the new design now depends on, and nothing reports it. The fallback should at least preserve the logger, or the mismatch should be surfaced.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being earlier in the chain, with no enforcement
findings.body: The rename moved the context enrichment out of the metrics middleware into a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware. LoggerMiddleware now emits pluginId, endpoint, dsName and similar fields only through the context. That only works if ContextualLoggerMiddleware is placed before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares. The removed doc comment ('this middleware should live at the top of the middleware stack') was the only warning about this ordering. Reordering the list, or enabling LoggerMiddleware in another stack, will silently strip those fields from logs.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests
findings.body: contextual_logger_middleware.go is a new file with an instrumentContext helper and eight middleware methods, but no test covers it. Nothing checks that the contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are attached for each endpoint, or that the optional DataSourceInstanceSettings and User branches behave correctly. The behaviour that moved from the metrics middleware and the LoggerMiddleware change are also untested. The LoggerMiddleware field change and the FromContext wrapper (pkg/plugins/log/logger.go) have no test either.

findings.title: Test function name still refers to the old InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the type is now MetricsMiddleware, but the test is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware. This keeps the old name in test output and makes it harder to find the test for the renamed type.
